column2: Why are inflammation and infection related but not interchangeable?
column3: Microbes can cause inflammation, but sterile infarction, crystals, trauma, autoimmunity and tumours can also cause it without any infection.

column3: Inflammatory signalling raises hypothalamic prostaglandin synthesis, lifting the defended temperature; chills reflect heat generation and conservation to reach the new set point.

column2: Why is resolution of inflammation described as active, and what happens if it fails?
column3: The stimulus must be removed, mediators decay, neutrophil recruitment stop and dead cells be cleared, with macrophages ingesting apoptotic neutrophils; failure at any step can sustain injury after the trigger has gone.
